slides.title: Does cycling or running make you faster?
slides.sub: What off skate training transfers, and what does not

slides.title: Engine transfers, pattern does not
slides.body: Heart, lungs and aerobic fitness carry over between sports. The sideways push on one skate barely carries over at all.

slides.title: What transfers to skating
slides.caption: Activities plotted by how much engine and how much skating pattern they give you.

slides.title: Cycling builds the engine
slides.body: Same big push muscles, a folded hip position and almost no impact. It cannot train single leg balance, lateral hip strength or push timing.

slides.title: Run easy and build slowly
slides.body: Running is convenient and good for bone. Keep most of it easy and away from key skating sessions. Tight calves mean too much.

slides.title: Copy the skating pattern
slides.body: Slide board, low walks, lateral bounds, single leg squats and imitation crossovers. Twenty minutes twice a week beats an extra hour of cycling for your corners.

slides.text: Cross training for inline speed skating is not a compromise.
